sectorLine: Industrials — Optical fibre & cable, copper foil, automotive systems
headlineHtml: Japan's most leveraged data-centre optics print: H1 operating profit tripled, and the guide now needs H2 to repeat it — on price as much as volume
ledeLeadHtml: Furukawa Electric is a 140-year-old wire, fibre and metals group — optical fibre and cable (incl. OFS and the Lightera fibre business), energy cable, copper foil and functional products, automotive wiring and batteries — whose legacy four-segment P&L (Electronics & Automotive Systems at 58% of sales) is being repriced by a single business: data-centre optics.
ledeHtml: In FY3/2026 net sales were ¥1,307,560mn, operating profit ¥63,856mn (4.9%), ordinary profit ¥75,858mn and owners' net income ¥72,514mn (EPS ¥1,030.2 pre-split; ¥103.02 post-split equivalent — Finnhub's annual EPS agrees), with net income flattered by ¥40,159mn of extraordinary income. FY3/2027 guidance has been raised twice, to sales ¥1,570,000mn / OP ¥136,000mn / owners' NI ¥118,000mn (9 November 2026). Strengths: (1) the optical inflection is extreme — H1 FY3/2027 OP tripled to ¥57.6bn (7.8% margin, an H1 record back to FY2001), with Optical Solutions OP swinging from ¥0.7bn to ¥23.6bn at an 18.0% margin on fibre/cable (+¥16.0bn of the OP bridge), specialty fibre and MT ferrules; (2) pricing power is documented, not hoped for — double-digit price revisions achieved, ~half the Optical full-year upgrade is price, and more than half of FY2028 optical-cable pricing is already effectively decided at revised levels (company Q&A); (3) Functional Products' HVLP copper foil (now over half of high-frequency-substrate foil) gives a second AI-hardware leg — FY3/2026 segment OP ¥15,379mn at 10.2%; (4) the plan is explicit — Vision 2030 targets FY2030 OP of ¥250bn (>10% margin), ¥200bn of it data-centre-related, with ROE 20% / ROIC 15%, and management floated the FY2028 ¥170bn milestone arriving a year early; (5) two guidance raises already this year with segment OP guides raised in Optical (+¥10bn to ¥53.0bn). Weaknesses: (1) the quality of the H1 sales beat is mixed — of the +¥127.0bn YoY sales increase, copper added +¥61.3bn and FX +¥33.0bn while substantive growth was +¥75.1bn (company bridge), and roughly half the Optical OP upgrade is price, partly cost pass-through; (2) the guide back-loads again — implied H2 OP is ¥78.4bn vs ¥57.6bn in H1 (calculated), and full-year free cash flow is guided to roughly zero despite ¥136bn of OP; (3) leverage is real — net debt of ¥246,188mn (calculated) at FY3/2026-end against a ¥650bn FY2026–30 investment plan (¥500bn to DC growth areas) that lands before the cash flow; (4) the legacy book is thin — Metal Solutions earned a 1.3% H1 margin, Service & Development has lost money in all ten years shown, and Infrastructure lost ¥11,252mn as recently as FY3/2024; (5) disclosure breaks are stacking up — a NEW five-segment classification applies from April 2026 (no restated history in the materials read), the sheet's regional rows proved positionally inconsistent across the FY2022/23 document-order change (corrected here from the tanshin texts — see Basis), and orders/backlog are not disclosed; (6) the stock has round-tripped violently — ¥1,982.5 on 16 November (−8.54% on the day) against a split-adjusted 52-week high above ¥50,000 pre-split equivalent in June 2026 per secondary data. Rating and price target are Under Review placeholders (see Basis of preparation).

bullets.leadHtml: Two raises, H2 still has to be bigger
bullets.html: FY3/2027 guidance: initial (12 May 2026) sales ¥1,460,000mn / OP ¥95,000mn → Rev.1 (6 August) ¥1,530,000mn / ¥123,000mn → Rev.2 (9 November) ¥1,570,000mn / OP ¥136,000mn / ordinary ¥155,000mn / NI ¥118,000mn, dividend ¥22 post-split. Of the Rev.2 sales raise, ~¥27bn of +¥40bn is copper-price effect (company). Implied H2 OP of ¥78.4bn (calculated) is 36% above H1 — the delivery question is now H2-weighted.

bullets.leadHtml: Optical Solutions is the whole story
bullets.html: H1 FY3/2027 (new segment basis): Optical Solutions sales ¥130.9bn, OP ¥23.6bn (18.0%) vs ¥0.7bn a year earlier — fibre/cable +¥16.0bn of the bridge, specialty fibre +¥5.5bn, MT ferrules +¥3.0bn, Broadband & Network −¥1.0bn (company Q&A). The full-year Optical OP guide was raised ¥10bn to ¥53.0bn, split ~¥4.5bn price / ~¥4.5bn mix. Multi-year contracts carry volume take-up guarantees and compensation clauses (company) — but locked contracts cannot be repriced, so FY2028 depends on the unlocked remainder.

bullets.leadHtml: Copper and FX did half the H1 work
bullets.html: Of H1's +¥127.0bn sales increase, the company's own bridge attributes +¥61.3bn to copper prices and +¥33.0bn to FX, with consolidation-scope changes (battery deconsolidation) subtracting ¥42.4bn — substantive growth was +¥75.1bn. The same pass-through mechanics that flatter the top line will reverse if copper falls; Metal Solutions (¥237.5bn of H1 sales) earned just 1.3%.

Vision 2030 (19 May 2026, company plan): FY2030 OP ¥250bn at >10%, ¥200bn from data-centre business, ROE 20%, ROIC 15%; FY2028 milestone OP ¥170bn; total investment FY2026–30 of ¥650bn, ¥500bn to growth areas. Against that: FY3/2027 FCF guided to roughly zero (H1 FCF +¥7.5bn), and net debt was ¥246,188mn (calculated) at FY3/2026-end. The plan is funded through the cycle it bets on.

bullets.leadHtml: A new segment map with no history
bullets.html: From April 2026 the group reports five segments — Optical Solutions, Digital Infrastructure Components, Energy Infrastructure, Automotive Systems, Metal Solutions — replacing the four-segment basis of Exhibit 2. No restated history on the new basis was in the materials read, so new-basis segment trends cannot yet be computed; the FY3/2027 segment OP guides (Optical ¥53.0bn, DIC ¥51.0bn, Energy ¥7.0bn) are the only full-year anchors.

blocks.heading: 1. Key indicators and financial history
blocks.html: Exhibit 1 (page 1) summarises ten fiscal years, FY3/2017–FY3/2026, all J-GAAP as originally reported. The decade is a long fade and a sudden repair: OP peaked at ¥44,804mn (4.6%) in FY3/2018, decayed to ¥8,429mn (1.0%) in FY3/2021 and ¥11,171mn (1.1%) in FY3/2024, then jumped to ¥47,097mn (FY3/2025) and ¥63,856mn (4.9%) in FY3/2026 as optics and copper foil inflected. Owners' net income follows the same arc (¥10,001mn in FY3/2021 → ¥72,514mn in FY3/2026), with FY3/2026 including ¥40,159mn of extraordinary income against ¥11,073mn of extraordinary losses. Operating cash flow was negative in FY3/2022 (−¥13,269mn) and nearly zero in FY3/2021 (−¥479mn) — the group's cash conversion has historically been as weak as its margins. Per-share figures cross a break: a 10-for-1 split took effect on 1 July 2026 (register S6); Exhibit 1 EPS is calculated on each year's pre-split weighted shares as printed, and FY3/2026 EPS of ¥1,030.2 equals ¥103.02 post-split (Finnhub's annual EPS agrees exactly).

blocks.heading: 2. Latest update — H1 FY3/2027 results and the second guidance raise
blocks.html: Q2 FY3/2027 results were published on 9 November 2026 with a full briefing presentation and a company Q&A summary (13 Q&As) — the richest interim disclosure set in this coverage. The print also introduced the new five-segment classification that applies from April 2026.

blocks.heading: H1 FY3/2027 results
blocks.html: H1 (April–September 2026) set first-half records at every line (company): sales ¥737.7bn (+20.8%), OP ¥57.6bn (+201.1%; 7.8% margin), ordinary profit ¥64.9bn, owners' net profit ¥58.8bn — the highest H1 since FY2001. The company's bridge decomposes the +¥127.0bn sales increase into copper +¥61.3bn, FX +¥33.0bn, scope changes −¥42.4bn (battery deconsolidation) and substantive growth +¥75.1bn; of the +¥38.5bn OP increase, volume/mix contributed +¥20.9bn (Optical Solutions +¥10.4bn, Digital Infrastructure Components +¥6.9bn), with price revisions on top. New-basis segments (Fact Book): Optical Solutions ¥130.9bn / ¥23.6bn (18.0%); Digital Infrastructure Components ¥118.9bn / ¥15.2bn (12.8%); Energy Infrastructure ¥69.9bn / ¥4.9bn (7.1%); Automotive Systems ¥188.9bn / ¥12.9bn (6.8%); Metal Solutions ¥237.5bn / ¥3.1bn (1.3%); Service & Development/adjustments −¥2.0bn of OP. Free cash flow was +¥7.5bn (OCF +¥28.7bn). Contract colour (Q&A): medium/long-term supply contracts are being written with volume take-up guarantees and monetary compensation; more than half of FY2028 optical-cable pricing is already effectively decided at revised levels; submarine-fibre capacity is planned to 4× the start-of-FY2026 level by FY2029; rollable-ribbon expansion runs FY2026–28.

blocks.heading: Guidance chain (Exhibit 3)
blocks.html: Initial (12 May 2026): sales ¥1,460,000mn, OP ¥95,000mn, owners' NI ¥82,000mn. Revision 1 (6 August 2026): sales ¥1,530,000mn, OP ¥123,000mn, NI ¥105,000mn. Revision 2 (9 November 2026): sales ¥1,570,000mn, OP ¥136,000mn, ordinary profit ¥155,000mn, NI ¥118,000mn; dividend unchanged at ¥22 post-split. (A separate 24 September 2026 notice revised only the H1 forecast.) Company-stated reason for Rev.2 (tracker): mainly data-centre-related product demand growth driving optical-solutions sales expansion; of the +¥40bn sales raise, ~¥27bn is copper-price effect (briefing). Segment OP guides: Optical Solutions raised +¥10bn to ¥53,000mn; Digital Infrastructure Components held at ¥51,000mn (sales cut ¥10bn to ¥315,000mn on a consolidation-elimination review — explicitly not demand); Energy Infrastructure held at ¥7,000mn; Automotive Systems +¥1bn; Metal Solutions +¥2bn. Implied H2 OP is ¥78.4bn (calculated) vs ¥57.6bn in H1, and full-year FCF is guided to roughly zero.

blocks.heading: 3. Business description
blocks.html: Furukawa Electric (founded 1884; headquartered in Marunouchi, Tokyo) is the Furukawa group's wire, fibre and metals house. President & CEO is Hideya Moridaira. Through FY3/2026 it reported four segments (segment profit = operating profit; register S3); from April 2026 it reports five (see section 5). A 10-for-1 stock split took effect on 1 July 2026.

blocks.heading: Electronics & Automotive Systems (legacy) → Automotive Systems / Metal Solutions / DIC (new)
blocks.html:
The legacy segment — automotive wiring harnesses and parts, batteries, electronic components, copper and aluminium wire — was 58% of FY3/2026 sales (¥756,170mn) at a 4.5% OP margin (¥33,887mn), rebuilt from ¥123mn of OP in FY3/2022. On the new basis it splits mainly into Automotive Systems (H1 FY3/2027: ¥188.9bn / ¥12.9bn, 6.8%), Metal Solutions (¥237.5bn / ¥3.1bn, 1.3% — copper products on pass-through pricing) and parts of Digital Infrastructure Components. The battery business was deconsolidated during FY3/2027 (H1 scope effect −¥42.4bn of sales, company bridge).

Digital Infrastructure Components carries the largest single assumption in the raised FY3/2027 guide. Its full-year operating-profit forecast was held at ¥51.0bn at the 9 November revision (sales were cut ¥10bn to ¥315bn on a consolidation-elimination review, explicitly not demand) after H1 delivered ¥15.2bn — implying ¥35.8bn in H2, a 2.4× half-on-half step-up across DFB laser chips, copper foil, memory disks and semiconductor tape. Within foil, HVLP4 copper foil for high-frequency substrates is now over half of that category (company Q&A). Metal Solutions, by contrast, earned ¥3.1bn on ¥237.5bn of H1 sales (1.3%): of the +¥40bn sales raise at Rev.2, about ¥27bn is copper price, so the segment's sales line inflates with the metal price while its margin remains the group's thinnest.

blocks.heading: Infrastructure (legacy) → Optical Solutions / Energy Infrastructure (new)
blocks.html:
Optical fibre and cable (OFS in the US; the Lightera fibre/cable business in Latin America), optical devices and components (MT ferrules, specialty fibre), telecom systems, and energy cable including submarine cable. Legacy FY3/2026: sales ¥363,941mn, OP ¥21,439mn (5.9%) — after a ¥11,252mn loss in FY3/2024. On the new basis, Optical Solutions is the group's profit engine (H1 OP ¥23.6bn at 18.0%; FY guide ¥53.0bn) while Energy Infrastructure runs at ~7% (H1 ¥4.9bn; FY guide ¥7.0bn), with the ¥100bn-class domestic HVDC interconnection opportunity contributing nothing before 2030 by the company's own briefing (pack).

The company itself decomposed the Optical Solutions swing at the 9 November 2026 Q&A. Of the roughly ¥23bn year-on-year increase in H1 segment operating profit (from ¥0.7bn to ¥23.6bn), optical fibre and cable contributed +¥16.0bn, specialty fibre +¥5.5bn and MT ferrules +¥3.0bn, while Broadband & Network subtracted ¥1.0bn. Of the ¥10.0bn full-year Optical upgrade to ¥53.0bn, about ¥4.5bn is price and about ¥4.5bn mix, with price effects pulled forward from Q4 into Q2; double-digit percentage price revisions were achieved in places, including cost pass-through. Management also stated that medium- to long-term supply contracts are being written with volume take-up guarantees and monetary compensation, and that for FY2028 optical cable pricing, more than half is already effectively decided at revised price levels, with the rest still fluid — the contracted share is the boundary between the durable and the cyclical parts of the 18.0% H1 margin.

blocks.heading: Functional Products and Service & Development
blocks.html: Functional Products — copper foil (incl. HVLP foil for high-frequency substrates, now over half that category per the Q&A), functional plastics, thermal products (liquid cooling; H1 shipments delayed by customer plant start-ups) — earned ¥15,379mn at 10.2% in FY3/2026, the legacy book's best margin. Service & Development etc. has lost money in every year of the ten-year window (−¥6,703mn in FY3/2026 on ¥36,644mn of sales).

blocks.heading: 4. Market and value chain
blocks.html:
Furukawa's value chain runs from materials (copper, glass preforms) through components (fibre, foil, ferrules, harnesses) to systems (submarine cable). Competitive sets: optical fibre/cable against Corning, Sumitomo Electric, YOFC and Prysmian in a documented fibre shortage; copper foil against Mitsui Mining & Smelting and Circuit Foil into AI-server substrates; harnesses against Yazaki and Sumitomo Wiring Systems. The strategic tension is capital: ¥500bn of the ¥650bn Vision 2030 investment is earmarked for DC growth areas whose returns depend on pricing that is only partly locked, while the legacy metals/automotive book (over half of sales) earns 1–7% and consumes working capital with copper prices. The company's contract strategy — take-up guarantees and compensation clauses in multi-year supply deals — is the disclosed mechanism for shifting cycle risk to customers; how much of the ¥500bn is covered by such contracts is not disclosed.

The external market frame is consistent with the company's capacity stance. FIELDNOTES' optical-modules/CPO industry report (16 November 2026), citing Precedence Research (September 2026), puts the global optical-cable market at US$18.5bn in 2025 rising to US$49.76bn by 2035, a 10.4% CAGR, and the broader data-centre cable market (optical, copper, AOC and DAC) at US$13.7bn in 2025 rising to US$37.52bn by 2035. Furukawa's disclosed capacity path is built into that demand: rollable-ribbon cable expansion runs FY2026–28 and submarine-fibre capacity is to reach 4× the start-of-FY2026 level by FY2029 (company Q&A, 9 November 2026). The same report notes the optical-transceiver market reached about US$23.9bn in 2025, up 55% year on year on AI-cluster demand (LightCounting series) — the demand pool to which Furukawa's fibre, ferrule and specialty-fibre lines are the upstream complement.

blocks.heading: 5. Segments and regions
blocks.html: Segment profit is operating profit. Two bases exist and are never spliced: the legacy four segments (FY3/2017–26, Exhibit 2 and the history block) and the new five segments from April 2026 (H1 FY3/2027 and segment OP guides only — no restated history in the materials read). Regional sales are customer-location, annual only; regional profit is not disclosed (register S4, S7). NOTE — sheet discrepancy: the sheet's main-block regional rows follow each tanshin's printed column order, which changed between the FY2022 and FY2023 documents, so the sheet's second and third regional rows swap identity (Asia ex-China vs North & Central America) between FY3/2022 and FY3/2023 despite register S4's header-mapping note. The regional figures in this report are taken from the tanshin texts directly (see Basis).

blocks.heading: 6. Financial statements summary
blocks.html: FY3/2026 (J-GAAP): sales ¥1,307,560mn, gross profit ¥229,814mn (17.6%, calculated), SG&A ¥165,958mn (12.7%), OP ¥63,856mn. Net non-operating income of ¥12,002mn (incl. equity-method and dividend income) gave ordinary profit of ¥75,858mn; extraordinary income ¥40,159mn less losses ¥11,073mn gave PBT of ¥104,944mn; total taxes of ¥29,047mn (a 27.7% effective rate, calculated) and NCI left owners' net income of ¥72,514mn — EPS ¥1,030.2 pre-split on 70.39mn basic shares (¥103.02 post-split). Operating cash flow was only ¥28,116mn against that profit; capex ¥52,126mn; D&A ¥43,218mn. Balance sheet at FY3/2026-end: cash ¥70,474mn; interest-bearing debt ¥316,662mn (register S5 definition, as corrected by S15) — net debt ¥246,188mn (calculated); receivables ¥266,458mn; inventories ¥210,896mn (as corrected by S16; 2.35 months of cost of sales, calculated); payables ¥140,543mn. R&D and employees are not presented in the tanshin (register S7).

blocks.heading: 7. Strategy and mid-term plan
blocks.html: The Management Policy toward Vision 2030 (19 May 2026, company plan) targets FY2030 operating profit of ¥250bn at a margin above 10% — ¥200bn of it from data-centre-related business — with ROE of 20% and ROIC of 15%. The interim milestone is FY2028 OP of ¥170bn at ~9%; at the 9 November 2026 briefing President Moridaira said that if the current pace continues the ¥170bn could 'come into view one year early' — a comment, not a revised plan (pack). Total investment for FY2026–30 is ¥650bn, of which ¥500bn to growth (DC) areas: submarine-fibre capacity to 4× by FY2029, rollable-ribbon expansion FY2026–28, foil and device capacity. Capital returns: FY3/2027 dividend guide ¥22 post-split, unchanged through both raises.

blocks.heading: 8. Other information
blocks.html: Corporate actions: 10-for-1 stock split effective 1 July 2026 (register S6); battery business deconsolidated during H1 FY3/2027 (scope effect −¥42.4bn of H1 sales, company bridge); new five-segment classification from April 2026. The shares fell 8.54% on 16 November 2026 to ¥1,982.5 (post-split) a week after the raise — secondary data show a split-adjusted 52-week range of ¥879.1 to a June 2026 high an order of magnitude above the current price (Finnhub, pre-split prints) — the market is pricing optical-cycle duration, not the print. Major shareholders are 未取得 in the sources used. Next results: Q3 FY3/2027, expected early February 2027.

blocks.heading: 9. Basis of preparation
blocks.html: Sources: the PL/segment sheet for Furukawa Electric (5801) in its final audited form (recv-annual-audit copy; register S1–S16, including three 17 November 2026 corrections applied in that copy: S14 history FY2019 debt cell, S15 FY2026 debt double-count in Q2/Q3/annual, S16 inventory double-count across all 30 periods). Main window FY3/2022–FY3/2026 plus the FY3/2017–FY3/2021 history block. Also used: the guidance tracker (56-company edition, 17 November 2026) and the interview pack for 5801 (Q2 FY3/2027 briefing text and Q&A summary, Fact Book, Vision 2030 policy document). REGIONAL FIGURES: the sheet's main-block regional rows are positional by each document's printed column order, which changed between the FY2022 document (Japan/China/Asia ex-China/N&CA/Other) and the FY2023 document onward (Japan/Asia ex-China/N&CA/China/Other); register S4 states the rows were header-mapped, but the stored values follow the printed order, so rows 2–3 swap identity between FY3/2022 and FY3/2023. This report's regional series were re-derived from the tanshin texts in the company folder (2022_FY.txt–2026_FY.txt, related-information notes) and are internally consistent; the discrepancy is flagged for the sheet programme. The new five-segment basis (from April 2026) is presented only where the company discloses it (H1 FY3/2027, segment OP guides); it is not spliced into the legacy series. The sheet's template 'Estimate' columns were not used. Calculated figures are labelled as such. Gaps （未取得 / not disclosed): order intake and backlog (not disclosed as a total); regional profit; units, capacity in physical terms beyond the briefing's multiples, and utilisation; R&D and employees in the tanshin; restated segment history on the new five-segment basis; the share of the ¥500bn growth investment covered by take-or-pay contracts; major shareholders. The share price is the 16 November 2026 close, post-split (StockAnalysis price history; StockInvest); market capitalisation is StockAnalysis's ¥1.35tn. P/E on FY3/2026 post-split EPS is 19.2x and on the Rev.2 guide EPS (¥167.6, calculated) 11.8x (both calculated). Rating and price target are 'Under Review' placeholders — no rating or target has been set by the analyst for this coverage, and nothing in this report is a forecast or a recommendation.
